Visible structural labels and groups: - Upper portion: H₂N, H, and several OH groups. - Central portion: interconnected oxygen-containing rings, with O and OH labels. - Lower portion: a nitrogen-containing sugar ring with N, NH₂, HO, and OH substituents. - Multiple stereochemical bonds are indicated by solid triangular wedges and hashed wedges. Molecular formula: C₂₀H₃₇N₃O₁₃ MW: 527.5 CAS No.: 14918-35-5 ## [Summary of destomycin A] Destomycin A (DM-A) is a aminoglycosid antibiotic obtained by the incubation of *Streptomyces rimofaciens*. For physicochemical properties, DM-A occurs as a basic white powder. It is freely soluble in water, in methanol and in ethanol, and practically insoluble in ether, in chloroform and in benzene. DM-A technical for a feed additive is a dark brown liquid. DM-A has an antibacterial effect on Gram-positive bacteria, Gram-negative bacteria and fungi. It prevents reduction in productivity due to *Ascaris suum* (the mechanism of the anthelmintic activity involves inhibition of vitelline coat formation of parasite eggs), and promotes the growth of pigs. Analogous (diastereomeric) antibiotics include hygromycin B, which was once designated as a feed additive but cancelled as of October 12, 2004. ### «Standards and specifications in the Act on Safety Assurance and Quality Improvement of Feeds» DM-A is a pure-grade antibiotic that was designated as a feed additive as of July 24, 1976. The deoxystreptamine antibiotics can be subdivided into several groups depending on the nature and number of carbohydrate substituents in the molecule and their distribution relative to the carbon atoms of the deoxystreptamine ring. The antibiotics characterised by the presence of only one substituent in the aglycone also include antibiotics of the destomycin series. In contrast to neamine and paromamine, the carbohydrate substituent in the molecules of these antibiotics is at the C(5) carbon atoms of the deoxystreptamine ring and the pyranose ring also has a substituent—destomic acid. This group includes hygromycin B, the antibiotic A-396-1 (SS-56-D), destomycins A, B, and C, and the antibiotics SS-56-C, and A-16316-C. Depending on the number of substituents in the aglycone, aminoglycoside antibiotics containing deoxystreptamine can be divided into two types.
